summary: The affine-graph selection and both depth bounds follow with no mathematical errors or gaps. The reused scalar shifted-centroid proof requires only an actual positive-volume convex fiber and its own positive directional variance, which are established here; its global predecessor symmetry and covariance hypotheses are not used in that scalar derivation. The finite-atomic construction applies to the original base probabilities on Z^n with Helly number 2^n. The positive cap bound proves each affine approximant belongs to its actual fiber, so convexity provides the required actual lattice lift. The sheared-normal calculation then bounds every halfspace at one point chosen independently of all normals. Singleton and lower-dimensional base support, both epsilon endpoints, beta=0, zero sheared normals, and the zero-volume branch introduce no exception. All reused objects and volume normalizations retain their declared meanings.
